chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If you fear that you will not be able to stand [for prayer] in the last part of the night, and there is an ailment with you or cold has befallen you, then pray and offer Witr from the beginning of the night while traveling."

key_terms.آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ: the last part of the night

ai.seo_question: When can a traveler pray Witr at the beginning of the night instead of the end?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a specific legal concession (rukhsah) for travelers suffering from illness or cold, permitting them to perform Witr and Tahajjud at the beginning of the night rather than delaying until the last third. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj) in acts of worship, ensuring that physical weakness does not become a barrier to maintaining spiritual connection during travel.
